blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Long-term conversational memory in multi-party settings requires more than retrieving relevant content from long-term conversations: it must distinguish who said what, whom each statement concerns, how individuals perceive one another, what information is shared by the group, and how states change over time. Recent studies on multi-party dialogue benchmarks show that existing general-purpose LLM memory systems tend to lose person and group relations or struggle to integrate clues distributed across members, groups, and time. Together, these issues reveal two core bottlenecks: message attribution and relational understanding in multi-party dialogue, and state reconstruction from interleaved histories. To address both, we propose SpeakerMem-R1 : its dual-track memory stores speaker-labeled verbatim messages and derived states organized into person-level and group-level views, then combines evidence from both tracks by entity, event, and time at query time. To reduce attribution and update errors during structured memory construction while enabling local deployment, we train Writer-R1 with SpeakerLevenshtein and speaker-conditioned GRPO. On GroupMemBench, SocialMemBench, and EverMemBench, SpeakerMem-R1 achieves binary accuracies of 47.9%, 69.2%, and 61.9%, respectively. The scores are 3.3, 12.4, and 9.4 percentage points over the best results of mainstream frameworks evaluated on each benchmark, respectively. On the publicly reported EverMemBench leaderboard from EverMind-AI, SpeakerMem-R1 achieves 62.33%, the best reported result among the latest state-of-the-art frameworks. It also achieves 70.85% on all 1,986 LoCoMo questions, which we use as a two-person long-term conversation boundary test. In a controlled evaluation of 305 questions, RL raises the SFT Writer’s mean accuracy from 57.38% to 68.20% under a frozen query/answer pipeline. We report both binary accuracy and token-F1, and ablations show that the verbatim and structured tracks, as well as person-level and group-level views, are complementary under the standardized evaluation interface. blocks.zh: 长期对话记忆在多党环境下需要的不仅仅是从长期对话中取回相关内容:它必须区分谁说出什么,每个声明都涉及谁,个人如何彼此认识,群体共享哪些信息,以及状态如何随时间变化. 最近关于多党对话基准的研究表明,现有的通用LLM记忆系统往往会失去人和群体关系或挣扎来整合分布在成员,群体,时间之间的线索. 这些问题共同揭示出两个核心瓶颈:多党对话中的信息归属和关系理解,以及从互不关联的历史中看出的国家重建。 为了解决这两个问题,我们提议Speaker Mem-R1:它的双轨记忆存储器 标有演讲者标签的逐字记录和衍生的状态,组织成人级和群级观点,然后按实体、事件和查询时间综合两个轨道的证据。 为了减少结构内存建设过程中的归属并更新出错,同时允许本地部署,我们用SpeakerLevenshtein和扬声器条件GRPO来训练Writer-R1. 在GroupMem Bench, SocialMem Bench, 和EverMem Bench, 演讲人上 Mem-R1分别实现47.9%,69.2%和61.9%的二进制速率. 得分分别为3.3分、12.4分和9.4分,高于每个基准评价的主流框架的最佳结果。 在EverMind-AI公开报道的EverMem Bench领导板上,SpeakersMem-R1取得了62.33%的成绩,这是最新最新最新框架中报告的最佳结果。 它还在所有1,986个LoCoMo问题上实现了70.85%,我们用它们作为两人长期对话的边界测试. 在对305个问题进行控制评价时,RL将SFT Writer的平均精度从57.38%提高到68.20%,在被冻结的询问/回答管道下. 我们报告二进制准确度和符号-F1,模拟显示,在标准化评价界面下,逐字记录和结构化轨道以及人级和集团级观点是相辅相成的。 项目网页:https://2022hpsk.github.io/ SpeakerMemR1 GitHub: https://github.com/2022hpsk/ SpeakerMemR1 关键词 : 多党对话; 长期对话记忆; 双轨记忆; 强化学习

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Long-term conversational memory enables language agents to retain facts, preferences, and social relations across sessions ( Zhong et al., 2024 ; Park et al., 2023 ; Packer et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) . Existing work mainly targets single-user or two-person histories, splitting, compressing, indexing, and retrieving conversations by relevance ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) . Multi-party group chats additionally contain speaker relations, reply structure, cross-topic branches, and state revisions, so they cannot be flattened into a message stream that is simply compressed in order ( Ghosal et al., 2019 ; Li et al., 2020 ) . GroupMemBench, SocialMemBench, and EverMemBench further show that general-purpose memory systems degrade substantially in multi-party or long-term conversation settings, while BM25 or dense retrieval can remain competitive in some configurations ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Owolabi, 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026b ) . The problem is therefore not merely finding relevant text, but preserving and recovering relations and historical structure in multi-party dialogue.
blocks.zh: 长期的对话记忆使语言代理人能够保留各种会议的事实、喜好和社会关系(钟等,2024;朴等,2023;Packer等,2023;Wu等,2025)。 现有工作主要针对单用户或双人历史,分出,压缩,索引,按关联性检索对话(Maharana等,2024;Wu等,2025.). 多党团体聊天还包含演讲者关系,回复结构,跨专题分会,以及状态修改等内容,因此不能被平整为简单按顺序压缩的信息流(Ghosal等,2019;Li等,2020. GroupMem Bench,SocialMem Bench,和EverMem Bench进一步显示,通用内存系统在多党派或长期对话的设置中大幅退化,而BM25或密集检索在某些配置中仍然可以保持竞争性(Yang等,2026;Owolabi,2026;Hu等,2026b.). 因此,问题不仅仅是找到相关案文,而是在多党对话中维护和恢复关系和历史结构。

blocks.en: We organize this problem around two coupled challenges: message attribution , which distinguishes who said what, whom the content concerns, and whether information is personal or shared; and state reconstruction , which recovers current or historical states from clues distributed across members, groups, and time ( Ghosal et al., 2019 ; Li et al., 2020 ; Owolabi, 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026b ) . Global relevance retrieval does not guarantee that a low-frequency member or the correct branch enters a limited candidate set, while summaries, fact aggregation, and generic memory graphs may lose source/owner, PERSON/GROUP scope, or state versions ( Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009 ; Karpukhin et al., 2020 ; Lewis et al., 2020 ; Zhong et al., 2024 ; Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Yue et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ; Tang et al., 2026 ) . Multi-party memory therefore needs verifiable evidence with participant relations and query-conditioned local state reconstruction, rather than simply more summaries or graph edges.
blocks.zh: 我们围绕两个相互关联的挑战来组织这一问题:信息归属,它区分谁说了什么、内容涉及谁、信息是个人的还是共享的;以及国家重建,它从分布在成员、团体和时间的线索中恢复当前或历史状态(Ghosal等,2019年;Li等,2020年;Owolabi,2026年;Hu等,2026年b)。 全球相关性检索不能保证低频成员或正确的分支进入有限的候选集,而摘要、事实汇总和通用内存图可能失去源/所有者、个人/GROUP范围或状态版本(Robertson & Zaragoza,2009年;Karpukhin等,2020年;Lewis等,2020年;Zhong等,2024年;Chhikara等,2025年;Yue等,2026年;Xu等,2026年;Gutierrez等,2024年;Tang等,2026年)。 因此,多方记忆需要与参与者关系和基于查询条件的本地国家重建的可核查证据,而不只是更多的摘要或图边.

blocks.en: Figure 1: A multi-party group chat is not a flat message stream: participants discuss different topic branches, express different positions, refer to one another, and revise earlier states. Flat retrieval, aggregate summaries, and generic graph structures can lose these relations. SpeakerMem-R1 preserves attribution and reconstructs state with dual-track memory and the Anchor–Separate–Resolve–Compose query procedure.

blocks.en: We propose SpeakerMem-R1 , a dual-track system that preserves speaker-labeled messages alongside provenance-linked derived states organized into person-level and group-level views. At query time, Anchor–Separate–Resolve–Compose retrieves and organizes evidence by participant, event, and time. We train a locally deployable Writer with SpeakerLevenshtein and speaker-conditioned GRPO to reduce attribution and update errors while freezing query and answer modules.

Compared with the best results of mainstream frameworks evaluated on each benchmark, the scores are higher by 3.3, 12.4, and 9.4 percentage points, respectively. On the publicly reported EverMemBench leaderboard from EverMind-AI, SpeakerMem-R1 achieves 62.33%, the best reported result among the latest state-of-the-art frameworks. blocks.en: Our contributions are as follows: • We design SpeakerMem-R1 , a dual-track memory system that combines traceable verbatim messages with person-level and group-level structured views for attribution, scope control, and state reconstruction in multi-party dialogue; • We provide an analysis framework derived from question requirements and recurring error patterns in three multi-party benchmarks, covering member coverage, information attribution, personal/group scope, term and event disambiguation, and temporal updates with multi-hop reasoning; • We train a locally deployable Qwen2.5-3B Writer with SpeakerLevenshtein and speaker-conditioned GRPO; on 305 controlled questions, RL writer reaches 95.4% of the LLM writer reference accuracy, while the dual-track design and writing objective are evaluated on three multi-party benchmarks, LoCoMo, and targeted ablations.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Long-term conversational memory and multi-party memory benchmarks. LoCoMo and LongMemEval evaluate factual, temporal, multi-hop, knowledge-update, and abstention abilities in long-term conversations ( Maharana et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ) ; MemBench, MemoryAgentBench, StoryBench, and REALTALK extend this scope to reflective memory, test-time learning, dynamic branches, and real-world interaction ( Tan et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2025 ; Wan & Ma, 2025 ; Lee et al., 2025 ) . In multi-party settings, DialogueGCN and Molweni establish the importance of speaker relations and discourse structure ( Ghosal et al., 2019 ; Li et al., 2020 ) , while GroupMemBench, SocialMemBench, and EverMemBench evaluate group dynamics, social relations and norms, and cross-group collaboration with evolving states ( Yang et al., 2026 ; Owolabi, 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026b ) . These benchmarks show that group-chat evidence is distributed and updated across members, groups, and time rather than reducible to a flat message sequence.
blocks.zh: 长期对话记忆和多党记忆基准. LoCoMo和LongMemEval评价长期对话中的事实、时间、多跳、知识更新和弃权能力(Maharana等,2024;Wu等,2025;Mem Bench, Memory Agent Bench, Story Bench, 和REALTALK将这一范围扩大到反思记忆、测试时间学习、动态分支和现实世界互动(Tan等,2025;Hu等,2025;Wan & Ma,2025;Lee等,2025)。 在多党环境中,对话GCN和Molweni确立了演讲者关系和言论结构的重要性(Ghosal等,2019;Li等,2020;GroupMem Bench, SocialMem Bench,和EverMem Bench),同时评价群体动态,社会关系和规范,以及与不断发展的国家的跨群体合作(Yang等,2026;Owolabi,2026;Hu等,2026b.). 这些基准表明,分组对话证据在成员、团体和时间之间分发和更新,而不是被简化为统一的信息序列。

blocks.en: Retrieval augmentation, structured memory, and memory graphs. BM25, dense retrieval, and RAG/REALM/RETRO provide lexical or semantic matching but generally do not constrain member coverage, information attribution, or event consistency ( Robertson & Zaragoza, 2009 ; Karpukhin et al., 2020 ; Lewis et al., 2020 ; Guu et al., 2020 ; Borgeaud et al., 2022 ) . MemoryBank, Mem0, A-MEM, MemGPT, generative agents, MemoBase, MemOS, and Zep study persistent facts, updates, connections, profiles, and temporal knowledge organization ( Zhong et al., 2024 ; Chhikara et al., 2025 ; Xu et al., 2025 ; Packer et al., 2023 ; Park et al., 2023 ; memodb-io, 2024 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Rasmussen et al., 2025 ) , whereas MemoryLLM and M+ write memory into latent spaces ( Wang et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025a ) . EverMemOS/EverOS, RippleMem, MIRIX, HippoRAG, RAPTOR, GraphRAG, LightMem, StructMem, Mnemis, HyperMem, and LightRAG further use consolidation, event graphs, multi-agent collaboration, recursive summaries, and graph or hypergraph retrieval ( Hu et al., 2026a ; EverMind researchers, 2026 ; Ji et al., 2026 ; Wang & Chen, 2025 ; Gutiérrez et al., 2024 ; Sarthi et al., 2024 ; Edge et al., 2024 ; Fang et al., 2026 ; Xu et al., 2026 ; Tang et al., 2026 ; Yue et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2024 ) . These methods improve compression and association, but do not necessarily preserve key information in multi-party group chats, such as message attribution, cross-person cognition, and group consensus, among other aspects.
blocks.zh: 检索增强,结构化内存,和内存图. BM25、密集检索和RAG/REALM/RETRO提供语法或语义匹配,但一般不限制成员覆盖、信息归属或事件一致性(Robertson & Zaragoza,2009年;Karpukhin等,2020年;Lewis等,2020年;Guu等,2020年;Borgeaud等,2022年;Mem0、A-MEM、MemGPT、基因剂、MemoBase、MemOS和Zep研究持久性事实、更新、联系、概况和时间知识组织(Zong等,2024年;Chhikara等,2025年;Xu等,2025年;Packer等,2023年;Park等,2023年;memodb-io,2025年; 2024;Li等,2025a;Rasmussen等,2025a;而记忆LLM和M+将记忆写入潜在空间(Wang等,2024;Wang等,2025a)。 EverMemOS/EverOS、RipleMem、MIRIX、HippoRAG、RAPTOR、GraphRAG、LightMem、StructMem、Mnemis、HyperMem和Light RAG进一步使用合并,事件图表,多代理协作,递归性摘要,并进行图谱或超图检索(Hu等,2026a;EverMind研究者,2026;Ji等,2026;Wang & Chen等. ; 2025; Gutiérrez等; 2024; Sarthi等; 2024; Edge等; 2024; Fang等; 2026; 徐等; 2026; 唐等; 2026; 岳等; 2026; 郭等; 2024. 这些方法改进了压缩和关联,但不一定在多党集团聊天中保存关键信息,如消息归属,人际认知,以及群体共识等.

blocks.en: Learnable memory management. Memory-R1, Mem- α \alpha , Agentic Memory, DeltaMem, and Memory-R2 learn memory actions, hierarchical construction, multi-step management, state-difference rewards, or long-horizon credit assignment ( Yan et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Yu et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ; Yan et al., 2026a ) . CoMAM jointly optimizes memory agents ( Mao et al., 2026 ) , and DeferMem trains query-time evidence distillation ( Yin & Tang, 2026 ) . In contrast, R 2 -Mem uses RL-free reflective search ( Wang et al., 2026 ) ; G-Memory organizes multi-agent experience in a hierarchy ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) ; Reflexion uses verbal feedback without updating model weights ( Shinn et al., 2023 ) . Our focus is owner-level writing supervision in group chats, training only the Writer while retaining fixed retrieval and answering modules.
blocks.zh: 学习记忆管理. Memory-R1, Mem- α\alpha, Agentic Memory, DeltaMem, and Memory-R2 学习记忆动作,分级构建,多步骤管理,国家分化奖励,或长视信用分配(Yan等,2026b;Wang等,2025b;Yu等,2026;Zhang等,2026;Yan等,2026a). CoMAM联合优化了内存代理(Mao等,2026年),DeferMem列车查询-时间证据分馏(Yin & Tang,2026年). 相形之下,R 2-Mem使用RL自由反射搜索(Wang等,2026年;G-Memory在分级中组织多剂体验(Zhang等,2025年;Reflexion使用口头反馈而未更新模型权重(Shinn等,2023年)). 我们的重点是在集体聊天中进行所有者级的写作监督,只培训作家,同时保留固定的检索和回答模块.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: The overall architecture is shown in Figure 2 . Given a multi-party message stream with speaker, time, and channel information, SpeakerMem-R1 first writes the messages into a traceable dual-track memory, then reconstructs query-specific evidence from the two tracks, and finally passes the evidence to a frozen answerer. The Writer is the component responsible for converting local messages into structured memory actions; the retrieval and answering stages operate on the resulting memory.
blocks.zh: 总体架构见图2。 鉴于一个多党派消息流带有扬声器,时间,和频道信息,SpeakerMem-R1首先将消息写入可追踪的双轨记忆,再从两轨重建出特定查询证据,最后将证据传递给被冻结的回答者. Writer是负责将本地消息转换为有条理的内存动作的组件;在所生成的内存上运行的检索和回答阶段.

blocks.en: Figure 2: Overall architecture of SpeakerMem-R1 . The system writes traceable System 1 verbatim memory and System 2 structures with participant, event, and state information, selects evidence from the two tracks at query time, and organizes it into the evidence set required for answering. RL rewards update only the Writer, while the answerer remains frozen.
blocks.zh: 图2:议长Mem-R1的总体结构 系统会用参与者,事件和状态信息书写可追踪的System 1逐字记录内存和System 2结构,在查询时间从两个音轨中选择证据,并将其组织成回答所需的证据集. RL奖励只更新了"作家",而回答者仍然被冻结.

blocks.en: 3.2 Five-Layer Traceable Dual-Track Memory
blocks.zh: 3.2 五层可追踪双轨存储器

blocks.en: SpeakerMem-R1 retains two complementary tracks. System 1 is the only verbatim layer and stores each message with its text, speaker, time, and channel. System 2 is a four-layer derived structure: PERSON-scoped Core (stable identity, facts, stances, and recurring behavior) and Profile (observations about a person or cross-person cognition), plus GROUP-scoped Interaction (cross-speaker events, relations, and decisions) and Insight (group norms, consensus, and exceptions). PERSON/GROUP fixes the record scope, source/owner separates who provides information from whom it concerns, and from_ids links every derived record to supporting messages. The verbatim track therefore supplies exact wording and local context, while the derived track supplies person-level and group-level state views; the full fields, code-level layer names, and query roles are given in Appendix Table 5 .

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: SpeakerMem-R1 uses a simple, efficient, and traceable dual-track memory to address the attribution and state-reconstruction failures that general-purpose memory systems exhibit in long-term multi-party conversations. It preserves source-linked verbatim evidence, organizes derived states into person-level and group-level views, and combines the two tracks through constrained query-time composition. This design directly targets multi-party memory failure modes without relying on a complex collection of additional mechanisms. Three multi-party benchmarks and LoCoMo demonstrate the design’s effectiveness and limits; ablations establish complementary contributions from the two tracks and person-level and group-level views. In the 305-question controlled study under the main protocol, the RL Writer (30 steps) reaches 95.4% of the 71.48 % 71.48\% LLM writer reference accuracy. This result shows that our RL method can make a locally deployable small Writer approach the performance of the large Writer while keeping the memory pipeline practical. Broader RL generalization, full-member coverage, cross-evidence reasoning, and knowledge outside memory remain open challenges.
blocks.zh: SpeakerMem-R1使用简单,高效和可追踪的双轨存储器来解决通用存储系统在长期多党对话中表现出的归属和状态重建失败. 它保存了源链接的逐字记录,将衍生状态组织为人级和群级视图,并通过受限制的查询-时间构成来将两个音轨结合起来. 这种设计直接针对多党内存失败模式,而不依赖于一系列复杂的附加机制. 三个多党派基准和LoCoMo显示了设计的有效性和限度;从两个轨道以及人一级和集团一级的观点中,制定补充性贡献。 在主协议下的305个问题控制研究中,RL Writer(30步)达到了71.48%的71.48%的LLM编剧参考精度的95.4%. 这一结果表明,我们的RL方法可以使本地可部署的小作家方法成为大型作家的性能,同时保持内存管道的实用性. 更广泛的RL通俗化,全员覆盖,交叉证据推理,以及外在记忆的知识仍然是公开的挑战.

blocks.en: The system assumes reliable rosters, source/owner attribution, and temporal identification; aliases, membership changes, implicit audiences, and parallel events remain challenging. Future work should reduce construction and retrieval cost and improve cross-evidence reasoning, open-domain QA, and generalization across domains and languages.

Total tokens include ingestion input, ingestion output, QA input, and final answer output, and exclude the judge stage; average tokens per question use the corresponding benchmark size as denominator. The three benchmarks contain 4,176 questions: 1,031 SocialMem, 745 GroupMem, and 2,400 EverMem. The SpeakerMem Writer can emit multiple update actions in one call, enabling small-batch ingestion; we therefore use the deployed configuration, with session-level ingestion for SocialMem and Window25 for GroupMem/EverMem. For Mem0, A-MEM, and HippoRAG, larger input chunks can reduce memory quality, so we use chunk5: each ingestion call processes five messages before the system performs memory merging, conflict resolution, and subsequent steps. This retains limited batching while avoiding the very high token cost of fully serial ingestion, and provides the cost-comparison setting reported here.

blocks.en: The Writer training set contains 15 multi-party networks and 73 writing segments (a writing segment is a Writer input unit, not the number of actions output by the model). To prevent sessions or windows from the same network appearing in both training and evaluation, train and held-out sets are separated at the complete-network level. We select the 10 shortest real SocialMemBench networks by message count, containing 50–101 messages, five sessions per network, and 5–12 terminal QA questions; they do not overlap with the 10 held-out SocialMemBench evaluation networks. We additionally use three manually authored UPDATE networks (30, 35, and 40 messages, covering state progression, UPDATE chains, source/owner separation, PERSON/GROUP scope, and temporal changes) and two manually authored NOOP networks (2–3 greeting or confirmation messages with no persistent fact).

blocks.en: Table 13 gives a reproducible inventory of the training networks. Although the training inventory contains only 15 complete networks, each network is processed through multiple Writer segments, yielding 73 writing segments, 89 terminal QA items, and 452 supervised actions (430 ADD, 20 UPDATE, and 2 NOOP). blocks.en: F.1 Five Analysis Dimensions: Definitions and Typical Errors
blocks.zh: F.1 五个分析层面:定义和典型错误

blocks.en: Here, the five dimensions form an analysis framework derived from question requirements and recurring error patterns; they are not independently human-annotated diagnostic labels. They organize related failure modes across the three benchmarks without defining a new validated taxonomy.
blocks.zh: 在此,这五个维度构成了从问题要求和反复出现的出错模式中衍生出来的分析框架;它们不是独立的人类附加说明的诊断标签. 它们将相关的失败模式组织在三个基准之间,而没有界定新的经过验证的分类。

blocks.en: The five dimensions are not mutually exclusive question labels and do not alter the original annotations of the benchmarks. We retain each benchmark’s official categories as quantitative reporting units, then map the dominant failure modes in each question to one or more diagnostic dimensions. The dimensions therefore explain why a question is missed rather than define a new aggregate score. The mapping uses the requirements in the question, object/scope/time constraints in the reference answer, and typical error cases, without additional manual gold labels beyond the test-set answers.
blocks.zh: 这五个方面并不是相互排斥的问题标签,也不改变基准的原始说明。 我们保留每个基准的官方类别作为定量报告单位,然后将每个问题的主要失败模式映射到一个或多个诊断层面。 因此,这些维度解释了为什么遗漏一个问题,而不是定义一个新的总分. 映射采用问题中的要求,参考答案中的对象/范围/时间限制,以及典型出错案例,除了测试-设定答案之外,没有额外的手工金色标签.

blocks.en: Questions asking for "every person", "all participants", or a group member list require evidence for every roster member or an explicit statement that information is missing. A typical error is that global top- k k retrieval returns only frequent members and misses infrequent or late-arriving members.
blocks.zh: 询问"每个人","所有参与者"或团体成员名单的问题,需要每个名册成员的证据或明确声明信息缺失. 一个典型的错误是,全球顶级- k k 检索只返回频繁成员, 并错过不频繁或迟到的成员。

blocks.en: Questions require distinguishing the message source (who provides or expresses it) from the owner (whom the content concerns), while preserving the direction of reports, evaluations, and stances. A typical error is rewriting Alice’s judgment about Bob as Bob’s self-report.
blocks.zh: 问题需要区分信息来源(谁提供或表达信息)和所有者(谁在内容方面令人关切),同时保留报告、评价和立场的方向。 一个典型的错误是将爱丽丝关于鲍勃的判断改写为鲍勃的自报.

blocks.en: Questions require distinguishing an individual preference or exception, a two-person relation, a multi-person event, and a group norm or consensus. Typical errors elevate a minority opinion to a group conclusion or use a group rule to overwrite an individual exception.
blocks.zh: 问题要求区分个人偏好或例外,二人关系,多人事件,以及群体规范或共识. 典型的错误将少数群体的意见提升为群体结论,或使用群体规则来覆盖个人例外。

blocks.en: Questions require locating the correct branch among same-named terms, similar topics, or parallel events using participants, channels, time, and verbatim clues. A typical error is merging different projects, meetings, or decisions into one event.
blocks.zh: 问题需要将正确的分支定位于同名名名词中,类似话题,或使用参与者,渠道,时间,和逐字记录线索的平行事件. 一个典型的错误是将不同的项目、会议或决定合并为一个活动。

blocks.en: Questions require selecting the requested point along a state-change chain and composing multiple pieces of evidence across members and events. Typical errors use an obsolete state as the current one or return only one fact from a chain without the connections needed for intermediate reasoning.
blocks.zh: 问题需要沿着国家变革链条选择所要求的点并汇集跨成员和事件的多件证据。 典型的错误使用过时状态作为当前状态,或者从一个链中只返回一个事实,而没有中间推理所需的连接.

blocks.en: This experiment examines how the two retrieval budgets jointly affect answer quality, distinguishing additional verbatim coverage from additional derived records. We reuse the fixed memory store constructed for the main experiments on SocialMemBench held-out eval10 (10 networks, 305 questions), using dual-track querying without ASK (for this sensitivity study, S1 recall- n n is set equal to S1 top- k k , so no larger candidate pool is recalled before Select). We evaluate all nine combinations of S1 top- k ∈ { 5 , 10 , 20 } k\in\{5,10,20\} and S2 k ∈ { 2 , 4 , 6 } k\in\{2,4,6\} , with S2 source_k =1 throughout. The two varied budgets concern S1 raw candidates and S2 owner/row retrieval, respectively; the source budget does not vary. No RL/SFT/Qwen Writer is used, so this is a retrieval-budget study with fixed memory. Acc is binary accuracy evaluated by GPT-4o-mini, and token-F1 is computed from per-question predictions and references. Both metrics are reported as percentages.
blocks.zh: 这一试验审查了两个检索预算如何共同影响答题质量,将额外逐字记录与额外衍生记录区分开来。 我们重新使用为SocialMem Bench hold-out eval10(10个网络,305个问题)上的主要实验而建造的固定内存库,使用双轨查询而不使用ASK(对于这一敏感度研究,S1 recept-n被设定为与S1上-k k相等,因此在Secto之前不会召回更大的候选池). 我们评价S1上-克的9个组合 {5,10,20}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ 两个不同的预算分别涉及S1原始候选人和S2所有者/行检索;源预算没有变化。 没有使用RL/SFT/Quen Writer,所以这是一个带有固定内存的检索-预算研究. Acc是由GPT-4o-mini评价的二进制精度,而令牌-F1则是从每个问题的预测和引用中计算出来的. 这两个指标都作为百分比报告。

Accuracy (left) and token-F1 (right) are plotted against S1 top- k k ; colors distinguish S2 k = 2 , 4 , 6 k=2,4,6 , and solid circles versus dashed squares identify the metrics. Panels use separate y-axis ranges to reveal smaller token-F1 changes; visual slopes should therefore not be compared across metrics. Outlined markers identify the best observed configuration for each metric. Lines connect measured configurations only. The setting uses the main-experiment memory store, 305 questions, no ASK, and S2 source- k = 1 k=1 .
blocks.zh: 图5:检索-预算响应曲线。 精确度(左)和符号-F1(右)相对为 S1 上-克;颜色区分为 S2 k = 2, 4, 6 k = 2, 4, 6, 和 实心圆相对被破碎的正方形表示度量. 面板采用单独的y轴范围来显示较小的符号-F1变化;因此,不应对各种度量衡的可视坡度进行比较。 外观标记确定每个度量的观测到的最佳配置. 行只连接被测量的配置. 设置使用主实验存储器,305个问题,没有ASK,S2源-克=1克=1.

blocks.en: S1 preserves original messages with speaker, time, and local context, supplying verifiable evidence for S2 records and wording that compression may omit. Increasing S1 top- k k from 5 to 10 and then to 20 improves both Acc and token-F1 at every tested S2 budget, indicating that small verbatim budgets still miss useful information. At S2 k = 4 k=4 , for example, Acc rises from 56.39% to 64.26% and 73.11%, while token-F1 rises from 23.85% to 25.00% and 26.53%. However, the first increment adds five candidate slots and the second adds ten, so their total gains alone do not measure diminishing returns. For S2 k = 2 , 4 , 6 k=2,4,6 , the average Acc gain per added S1 slot falls from 2.03, 1.57, and 1.25 percentage points over 5–10 to 0.89, 0.89, and 0.56 over 10–20. Thus, returns per S1 budget slot slow markedly, suggesting a trend toward saturation : after high-value messages have been covered, additional candidates may increasingly repeat existing evidence or contribute weaker clues. Total Acc gains over 10–20 remain 5.58–8.86 points, while token-F1 marginal gains are smaller and less uniform.
blocks.zh: S1用扬声器,时间,以及本地上下文保存了原始消息,为S2记录和压缩可能省略的措辞提供了可核查的证据. 将S1顶级-kk从5个增加到10个,然后增加到20个,在每一个经过测试的S2预算上,Acc和sord-F1都有改进,表明小逐字记录预算仍然缺少有用的信息. 例如,在S2克=4克=4时,Acc从56.39%上升到64.26%和73.11%,而象征-F1则从23.85%上升到25.00 %和26.53%. 然而,第一次递增增加了5个候选人名额,第二次增加10个候选人名额,因此仅靠这些候选人的总收益并不能衡量回报的减少。 对于S2克=2分,4分,6克=2分,4分,6分,每增加S1个槽的平均Acc增益从5-10分的2.03分,1.57分和1.25分下降到0.89分,0.89分和10-20分的0.56分. 因此,每个S1预算档次的回报明显缓慢,表明一种饱和趋势:在高价值信息被涵盖之后,其他候选人可能越来越多地重复现有证据或造成线索更弱。 Acc在10至20年的总收益仍为5.58至8.86分,而象征-F1的边际收益则更小而不太统一.

blocks.en: S2 supplies addressable derived states constrained by PERSON/GROUP scope, source/owner, event, and time. Increasing S2 k k from 2 to 4 improves both metrics at all three S1 budgets: Acc gains are 7.21, 4.92, and 4.91 points, and token-F1 gains are 0.96, 1.44, and 0.65 points. This is consistent with a moderate expansion recovering complementary participant, relation, and state clues. Increasing S2 further from 4 to 6 is less reliable. At S1 top- k = 10 k=10 , Acc rises only from 64.26% to 65.57%, while token-F1 falls from 25.00% to 24.75%. At S1 top- k = 20 k=20 , Acc falls from 73.11% to 71.15% and token-F1 from 26.53% to 25.78%, decreases of 1.96 and 0.75 points, respectively. One explanation consistent with the dual-track design is that excess derived records introduce duplicate facts, overlapping descriptions, or weaker relational and historical clues, diluting decisive evidence and increasing the answerer’s judgment burden. S2 should therefore retain a moderate set of complementary records rather than maximize quantity. The decline is directly observed; redundant or distracting records are one plausible mechanism.
blocks.zh: S2用品可处理的衍生状态受个人/GROUP范围、来源/所有人、事件和时间的限制。 将S2 kk从2个增加到4个改进了所有三个S1预算的衡量标准: Acc增收为7.21分,4.92分,4.91分;而平分-F1增收为0.96分,1.44分,0.65分. 这与适度扩张恢复补充参与者,关系,和状态线索一致. 将S2从4型进一步增加至6型不太可靠。 在S1顶级-克=10克=10分,Acc只从64.26%上升到65.57%,而正牌-F1从25.00%下降到24.75%. 在S1上-克=20克=20分,Acc从73.11%下降到71.15%,而正信-F1从26.53%下降到25.78%,分别下降了1.96分和0.75分. 一种与双轨设计相一致的解释是:过多的衍生记录引入了重复的事实,重复的描述,或者更弱的关系和历史线索,淡化了决定性的证据并增加了回答者的判断负担. 因此,S2应保留一套适度的补充记录,而不是尽量增加数量。 下降是直接观察到的;冗余或分散注意力的记录是一个可信的机制。

blocks.en: Figure 6: Joint S1/S2 configuration grid. The horizontal axis enumerates discrete S1 top- k k settings and the vertical axis gives S2 k k . Each cell reports exact percentages: the upper-left blue triangle encodes Acc and the lower-right rose triangle encodes token-F1. Independent color scales prevent direct cross-metric comparisons of shade. The outlined cell, ( 20 , 4 ) (20,4) , is the best observed configuration for both metrics. These are the same nine observations as Figure 5 , not a separate experiment.

blocks.en: Figure 6 shows that the effect of extra S2 budget depends on S1. With S1 top- k = 5 k=5 , increasing S2 from 4 to 6 still improves Acc/token-F1 from 56.39/23.85 to 59.34/24.35, consistent with additional derived clues filling gaps in limited raw coverage. The same S2 increment decreases both metrics when S1 top- k = 20 k=20 : once S1 supplies more complete original evidence, the complementary value of additional structured records may no longer outweigh redundancy and distraction. This pattern supports separate budget control for the two tracks. S1 expands verifiable verbatim coverage, while S2 should provide a compact set of query-relevant states and relations. It also fits Anchor–Separate–Resolve–Compose: attribution, scope, and versions are constrained before evidence is composed, and the two budgets need not be maximized together.
blocks.zh: 图6显示额外S2预算的影响取决于S1. S1顶级-克=5克=5,将S2从4个增加到6个仍能改进Acc/token-F1从. 56.39/23.85至59.34/24.35,与填补有限原始覆盖面空白的其他衍生线索相一致。 当S1上-克=20克=20时,同样的S2增量会减少两个度量:一旦S1提供更完整的原始证据,额外结构化记录的补充价值可能不再超过冗余和分心. 这种模式支持对两条轨道分别进行预算控制. S1扩展可核查的逐字记录,而S2应提供一套紧凑的与查询相关的状态和关系. 这也符合Anchor-Separate-Resolution-Compose:在形成证据之前,归属、范围和版本都受到限制,而且两个预算不必一起最大化。

blocks.en: Acc assesses task-level correctness, whereas token-F1 measures surface token overlap, so the metrics need not move together. With S1 top- k = 10 k=10 , increasing S2 from 4 to 6 raises Acc but lowers token-F1. A single metric could therefore overlook changes in answer completeness, concision, or wording, although this discrepancy alone cannot identify the responsible factor. Among the nine configurations, S1 top- k = 20 k=20 and S2 k = 4 k=4 jointly maximize Acc (73.11%) and token-F1 (26.53%), suggesting a useful quality balance between sufficient verbatim evidence and a moderate structured budget. This is the best observed quality balance in the tested grid; the main experiments retain S1 top- k = 10 k=10 and S2 k = 2 k=2 /source- k = 1 k=1 . Overall, the results favor monitoring marginal S1 returns and keeping S2 moderate.
blocks.zh: Acc 评估任务级别正确性,而sorder-F1 度量表令牌重叠,因此度量衡不需要一起移动. 以 S1 顶级-克 = 10 k = 10,将 S2 从 4 起升至 6 起升 Acc 但更下调 sorders-F1. 因此,单一的衡量标准可以忽略答案完整性、精度或措辞的变化,尽管这种差异不能单独确定责任因素。 在9个配置中,S1上-克=20克=20克和S2克=4克=4共同最大化Acc(73.11%)和道克-F1(26.53%),表明在充分逐字记录和适度结构化预算之间保持了有益的质量平衡. 这是被测试网格中观测到的质量最平衡;主实验保留了S1上-克=10克和S2克=2克=2克/出自-克=1克=1克. 总的来说,结果有利于监测S1的边际返回并保持S2的中度。
